newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open flat, market awaiting jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open flat, market awaiting jobs data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened almost unchanged in very quiet trade on Thursday, with investors cautious ahead of the release tomorrow of key Canadian and U.S. jobs data, analysts said.

"Nobody wants to do a whole lot ahead of payrolls tomorrow, which because of the seasonals could be anything," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.01 to C$112.21 to yield 7.019 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 13 basis points from 14 basis points on Wednesday.
Statistics Canada on Friday will release the country's employment report for May, while the United States will release its non-farm payrolls report for the same month.
Fixed-income investors will be studying the employment reports for evidence of inflation growth in both countries, and clues about whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will soon hike rates.

Analysts said the only area of significant activity in the Canadian bond market was the rebound in real return bonds following the poorly received auction of C$500 million in 4.25 percent real return bonds due 2026 yesterday.
Several market watchers described the auction as "disastrous" and said the Bank of Canada greatly overestimated demand for the issue.
This morning, Canada's 4.25 percent real return bond due December 1, 2021 rose C$0.38 to C$98.63 to yield 4.342 percent.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond dropped C$0.05 to C$105.37 to yield 6.508 percent, while the U.S. 10-year slipped 4/32 to 6.64 percent.
The negative spread widened to 13 basis points from 11 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.90 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.07 percent.
